propositions: The review bot must be cut over from direct Anthropic API to Bedrock inference profiles without cross-provider fallback, so that rebar dogfoods the path its clients use and surfaces Bedrock-specific failures before clients encounter them.

The cutover is purely additive (setting three class-slot env vars in compose) and purely subtractive for recovery (deleting those lines restores the Anthropic path), with no source code changes required.

The Bedrock provider package must be installed in the review-bot container image via --extra bedrock in the uv sync line, because without it the first Bedrock call raises LLMConfigError and silently halts the LLM-Review gate that votes on every landing on main.

The safety net (kill-switch runbook entry, Bedrock client-error alarm applied and observed on real data, induced VOTER_ERROR on the Anthropic path) must be proven before the cutover takes effect, enforced by commit ordering and operator-attested observations.

The cutover must preserve the per-pass model split (frontier on opus, standard and trivial on sonnet) through independent class-slot env vars rather than a single REBAR_LLM_MODEL, which would collapse the split that now exists.

End-to-end live production evidence must show every LLM call resolved to a bedrock: inference profile with zero direct-Anthropic calls, via the REBAR_USAGE_LOG tally; the per-pass class resolution verified in the vote sidecar provenance; and a kill-switch execution restoring the Anthropic path with a real vote, proving the credential works.
